ai.purpose: RTT/3 engine layer for Evolutionary Biology: triadic-substrate integration, multi-regime simulation hooks, lineage-aware reasoning, and hybrid-canon scaffolding.

engine.description: Integrates Evolutionary Biology into the full triadic substrate, enabling multi-regime reasoning, lineage tracking, and hybrid-canon simulation.

mapping.structure: Lineage maps to substrate memory channels that preserve adaptive information across generations.
mapping.variation: Novelty arises from perturbations in substrate-level encoding and developmental pathways.
mapping.selection: Environmental resonance patterns filter lineage trajectories based on fit.
mapping.adaptation: Stable resonance alignment between lineage and environment emerges over repeated cycles.

constraints: Lineage continuity is required for adaptive resonance.
Substrate-level invariants limit mutation and variation pathways.

R1.behavior: Primitive replicator dynamics; minimal lineage memory; high stochasticity.
R1.notes: Adaptive resonance weak; dominated by noise and drift.

R2.behavior: Genetic and molecular mechanisms partially stabilize adaptive patterns.
R2.notes: Lineage memory strengthens; variation becomes structured.

R3.behavior: Full population-level adaptive resonance; stable selection and lineage propagation.
R3.notes: Evolution expresses coherent, multi-generational adaptive cycles.

hooks.name: adaptive_resonance_sim
hooks.description: Simulates variation → selection → inheritance cycles as substrate-driven resonance loops.

hooks.name: lineage_memory_sim
hooks.description: Models how genetic and epigenetic memory stabilize adaptive patterns.

hooks.name: environmental_resonance_sim
hooks.description: Simulates how environmental constraints shape selection gradients and adaptive basins.

simulation.notes: Simulations operate on resonance patterns and lineage structures, not on metaphysical or teleological assumptions.

hybrid_canon.purpose: Enable agentic AIs to reason across biological, ecological, and informational modules using shared substrate invariants.
